newsitem.title: CONGO: Relatives of Mobutu and associates flee Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Relatives of Mobutu and associates flee Zaire.

text.p: A brother and a son of President Mobutu Sese Seko and relatives of members of Zaire's central government have joined a growing exodus in the face of rebel advances in the east, police in neighbouring Congo say.

In Lubumbashi, capital of Zaire's southern mining province of Shaba, sources in the foreign community said that central government officials there and army officers had flown family members to South Africa on a special flight on Wednesday.
Police sources in Brazzaville, across the Zaire River from Zaire's teeming capital Kinshasa, said Mobutu's son, Kongolo, had been in the Congo's capital since Thursday.

They did not name the Mobutu brother who was there but said that children of Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister General Lukulia Bolongo and of former Mobutu security adviser Seti Yale were in Brazzaville.
Ida Victorine Nze, president of the Congolese Red Cross, told reporters on Tuesday that Zaireans arriving in Brazzaville feared that events back home could take a turn for the worse.
She said the local Red Cross was "overstretched" by the exodus, which included many ordinary families. Church sources said 85 Zaireans had arrived on Monday.
Travel agents in Kinshasa say flights out of Zaire are fast booking up, with Europe and South Africa popular destinations.
In Lubumbashi, Zaire Airlines confirmed that a non-scheduled flight had taken 65 Zaireans to Johannesburg on Wednesday. They were "probably Easter holidaymakers", a spokesman said.
Earlier, 25 Lebanese women and children arrived in South Africa on a private charter from Lubumbashi.

Diplomatic sources said on Tuesday that small groups of Americans living in Kinshasa had started arriving in Brazzaville, complaining of harassment by Zaireans accusing Washington of supporting the rebels.
In Washington, the Pentagon said U.S. military specialists were on their way to Congo and Gabon to prepare the ground for any future evacuation of American citizens from Zaire.

France said it too was taking measures to protect its citizens. "We are in close communication with our European and American partners," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said in Paris on Wednesday.
Germany advised its citizens to leave Zaire.
Mobutu is in Europe, where he has spent most of his time since cancer surgery there in August. A spokesman said he would leave hospital in Monaco on Thursday following fresh treatment.
Airport sources in the French town of Nice said his plane was on stand-by to take him home. No departure date was set.

The rebels, fighting to overthrow Mobutu, captured Zaire's third largest city of Kisangani on Saturday. They have advanced in the east and south. A much-heralded army January 20 offensive proved a flop.
